structure: CSharp EmitHeapAllocate centralizes platform capability checks, allocation and null trapping. SLG emitArrayHeapBacking directly writes a malloc call for positive byte length, and uses a null pointer for zero length.
branches: For the actual4800-byte original42 path, CSharp uses Windows GetProcessHeap/HeapAlloc via sollang_alloc, then an explicit nonnull compare and trap edge. Current SLG uses CRT malloc without the corresponding emitted null-guard edge. Zero-length behavior and other targets require separate source comparison before changes.
cleanup: CSharp fixed backing cleanup calls sollang_free; Windows implementation checks null and calls HeapFree. Current SLG promoted backing cleanup extracts the descriptor data and calls CRT free. Normal allocation/release audits pass but do not prove platform allocator or allocation-failure parity.
finding: The difference is not established as cosmetic. Original42 common LLVM checks remain authoritative; the uncommitted SLG override was withdrawn following the user correction. No allocator implementation was changed yet.
next: Inventory shared allocation/reallocation/free consumers and compare CSharp platform-specific decisions before modifying the shared SLG implementation. Do not patch only original42, rename SSA solely to satisfy a literal assertion, or add producer-specific acceptance as a substitute.
